expected_text_segments:
Update: Gold before the jobs report: beyond the Fed's target range

Treasury's nominal yield fell 5 basis points on November 4. Its real yield fell 1. Gold's jobs-report watch needs both.

What to watch: A sustained real-yield rise after the jobs report would weaken this particular support for gold.

Read the full brief: https://capitalchronicle.substack.com/p/gold-before-the-jobs-report-beyond

Analysis, not financial advice. Readers decide whether to trade.

Capital Chronicle may hold positions in the markets it covers.

media_manifest.alt_text: Two bars compare the latest daily decline: 5 basis points for the nominal 10-year yield, and 1 basis point for the real 10-year yield. Zero is the baseline.
media_manifest.attribution: U.S. Department of the Treasury. Independent chart: Capital Chronicle.
media_manifest.caption: From 3 to 4 November, the nominal 10-year par yield fell 5 basis points and the real 10-year yield fell 1 basis point. A basis point is 0.01 percentage point. Sources: [U.S. Department of the Treasury](https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2026); [U.S. Department of the Treasury](https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_real_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2026).
media_manifest.placement_after: The latest fall was mostly nominal
